britannica-1911-abul-fazl:
Abul Fazl (1551-1602) was wazir, chief minister, and official historian to Akbar, the great Mogul emperor of India. The Britannica entry argues that his brilliant career as a minister would likely be forgotten without the record he wrote himself. That record, in Persian, is the Akbar Nameh, or Book of Akbar.

Two parts make up the work. The first gives a complete history of Akbar's reign, while the second, the Ain-i-Akbari, describes the religious and political constitution and the administration of the empire. Francis Gladwin's translation of the Ain appeared at Calcutta in the 1780s. Abul Fazl was assassinated in 1602, at the instigation of Prince Selim.
